requiredChecks: cd platform_v2/cloudflare_shadow && npm run materialize:original-ui:dry-run -- --target-env staging

workflowMarkers: public map snapshot alert lifecycle smoke

notes: Cloudflare staging is the promotion gate for Cloudflare production changes.
The staging public entrypoint is Cloudflare Worker ikimon-life-cloudflare-staging, not the legacy VPS staging runtime.

The Cloudflare command bus owns SHA pinning, release-candidate verification, environment approval, and status reporting; operational release logic is owned by scripts/run_cloudflare_staging_release.sh.
The portable release script runs in a fresh Cloudflare Sandbox for each job and does not depend on GitHub Actions or a controlled workstation.
D1 migrations are never executed by the staging deploy entrypoint; migration is a separate approval-bound job.
Routine releases reuse the existing staging write secret. Secret mutation is explicit through SYNC_STAGING_WRITE_SECRET=true.
Browser evidence is not duplicated in normal staging releases. PR CI selects affected browser surfaces; BROWSER_QA=full remains available for release evidence.

The staging Worker owns the staging.zukan.earth custom domain and retains staging.ikimon.life/* as the rollback-compatible route; it uses non-production shadow D1/R2 resources plus ikimon-staging-media-jobs.
Routine Cloudflare staging deploy must not use VPS SSH, /var/www/ikimon.life-staging, or VPS_SSH_KEY.
Production Worker config must not own staging.zukan.earth or staging.ikimon.life routes.
Legacy VPS staging remains only for old integration jobs until those jobs are migrated or retired.
releaseGates currently documents the legacy VPS verify_level=full gate; Cloudflare staging uses requiredChecks and public route smoke until the Postgres-only smoke is migrated to D1.
